Maximum number of legend characters per line for given plot dimensions

legendWidthFromPlotDimensions.Rd

Calculates the maximum number of characters per line that fit into the legend of a plot with the given exported dimensions - the maxWidth to be used with wrapLegendLabels().

The calculation is based on:

  • the legend position of the plot: legends on the left or right side are given at most legendFractionHorizontal of the total plot width (default 40%), legends at the top or bottom are given legendFractionVertical (default 100%);

  • the legend font size;

Usage

legendWidthFromPlotDimensions(
  plotObject,
  plotWidth = NULL,
  unit = NULL,
  dpi = NULL,
  legendFractionHorizontal = 0.4,
  legendFractionVertical = 1
)

Arguments

plotObject

A ggplot object, e.g. created by plotTimeProfile(), or a CombinedPlot object whose main plot is used.

plotWidth

Width of the exported plot. If NULL, the default export width option exportWidth is used.

unit

Unit of plotWidth: one of "cm", "in", "mm" or "px". If NULL, the default export width option exportUnits is used.

dpi

Resolution in dots per inch; used to convert plotWidth to physical inches when unit = "px". If NULL, the default export DPI option exportDpi is used.

legendFractionHorizontal

Maximum fraction of the total plot width available to legends on the left or right side. Ignored for top/bottom legends.

legendFractionVertical

Maximum fraction of the total plot width available to legends on the top or bottom side. Ignored for left/right and inside legends.

Value

A single integer, the maximum number of characters per legend line (at least 1).

See also

Other legend helpers: wrapLegend(), wrapLegendLabels()

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  time = 1:10,
  concentration = (1:10)^2,
  output = rep("Organism|PeripheralVenousBlood|Aciclovir|Plasma", 10)
)
p <- plotTimeProfile(
  data = df,
  mapping = aes(x = time, y = concentration, color = output)
)
# legend on the right may use 40% of an 8 cm wide plot
legendWidthFromPlotDimensions(p, plotWidth = 8, unit = "cm")
#> [1] 18

# bottom legend may use the full plot width
pBottom <- p + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
legendWidthFromPlotDimensions(pBottom, plotWidth = 8, unit = "cm")
#> [1] 46
